# looot-lookalike

> Open-source lookalike company search. 3 to 20 seed domains in, a ranked list out, each score explained by signal, weight, provider and cost. Data comes from looot (https://looot.ai), one token, pay per call.

## Run

- Demo, no token: `npm run demo` (web UI on http://localhost:3230) or `npm run lookalike -- --demo`
- Price only: `npm run lookalike -- --domains a.com,b.com,c.com --dry-run`
- Real run: `LOOOT_TOKEN=... npm run lookalike -- --seeds seeds.txt --cap 1 --out results-out`

## Setup

Node 22.12 or newer. `npm install --ignore-scripts`. The CLI reads `LOOOT_TOKEN` from the shell, not from .env.local (create a token in looot Settings, Agent tokens; a funded balance is needed for real runs). Copy weights.example.yaml to weights.yaml. examples/seeds.txt shows the seeds format. See README headings What you need, Run it with your own data, Weights file, Spending, Troubleshooting.

## Files

- weights.example.yaml: scoring weights and options
- src/lib/sources.ts: the looot endpoints and list prices used
- src/lib/score.ts: the score and its breakdown
- src/lib/engine.ts: quote, cap, idempotency keys, pending runs
- skills/looot-lookalike/SKILL.md: Claude Code skill

## Rules

- The cap is per run (`--cap`, default $1). Calls that would cross it are skipped.
- A call still running when waiting stops is "pending", not failed.
- A signal with no data is left out of the score and shown as lower coverage. Nothing is guessed.
- Output: lookalikes-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.json, .csv and .md.
